title: The Score for a Vanishing Sound
logline: A drumming teacher passes on a rhythm as spoken syllables before letting a student near the drum, a way of writing down, in sound, something that happens too fast to see.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The moment-by-moment rhythm of work becomes a rhythm taught aloud: a drumming teacher passing on, in spoken syllables, something too fast to watch.

thread_out.thread: Something too fast to watch becomes something too fast to replay: an umpire's split-second ruling while a whole ground waits in silence.

requirements: A traditional drumming teacher and apprentice household willing to be filmed over real lessons
Good sound recording conditions for the syllables and the drum
Consent that respects a hereditary tradition and does not exoticise it

suggestions.name: A traditional Kandyan drumming (bera) teaching household
suggestions.why: Kandy is closely associated with traditional drumming and its teaching lineages.
suggestions.verify: A specific teacher, student and willingness to be filmed are unconfirmed.
